takeaway: Scar strength after uncomplicated healing: about 10% at 1 week, rising rapidly over 4 weeks, then plateauing at 70-80% of unwounded skin by 3 months.

question.text: After 3 months of normal healing, about how strong is the scar as a percentage of the original undamaged skin?

lines.text: This is a scar's strength over time.
At one week the wound is weak, only about ten percent of normal skin.
lines.say: At one week the wound is weak, only about ten percent of normal skin.

lines.text: Over the next four weeks, tensile strength rises rapidly.
By three months it reaches a plateau.
On the gauge, that is seventy to eighty percent of unwounded skin.
After this point there is little further gain, as the note says.
So even a perfect repair never quite matches the original skin.
lines.say: (sigh) So even a perfect repair never quite matches the original skin.
